title: High server load
body: Hello. Thanks for the incredibly cool library. Respect. For the company's internal needs, I made an integration with the library, there are only about 12 connections (we tested it with 23), and the server is loaded quite heavily every 5-10 hours. What configuration methods are there to prevent this from happening? I read in the documentation that using a database, the load will not be so great, but still, the swap is almost always full and all the memory is used by all processes, although the accounts are actively used only once every 5 minutes and the scripts themselves are fast. This is what it looks like in htop: The settings I use: ``` public function getApiConnect($account = null): API { $path = dirname(__DIR__, 2).'/var/log/'; $settings = (new Settings) // Починаємо з загальних налаштувань ->setAppInfo( (new AppInfo) ->setApiId($this->parameterBag->get('tdlib_api_id')) ->setApiHash($this->parameterBag->get('tdlib_api_hash')) ) ->setLogger( // Додаємо налаштування логування (new Settings\Logger()) ->setMaxSize(100 * 1024 * 1024) // Максимальний розмір файлу логів 100MB (за бажанням) ->setExtra($path.'MadelineProto.log') ) ->setDb( (new \danog\MadelineProto\Settings\Database\Mysql) ->setUri('tcp://'.$this->parameterBag->get('danog_host')) ->setDatabase($this->parameterBag->get('danog_database')) ->setUsername($this->parameterBag->get('danog_username')) ->setPassword($this->parameterBag->get('danog_password')) ->setEnableFileReferenceDb(true) ->setEnableMinDb(true) ->setEnableUsernameDb(true) ->setEnableFullPeerDb(true) ->setEnablePeerInfoDb(true) ) ; return new API($this->getPathSession($account), $settings); } ``` By the way, if you don't set SetEnable, for some reason there are problems with access, although they seem to be true by default (observation).

title: Using MadelineProto for private server deployments
body:
Hello,

I'm currently trying to make a client work with a custom telegram server for research purposes.
I stumbled upon this client, which seems to provide everything I need (secret chats, basically), but the issue is that it looks like IP addresses and public key(s) of the servers are hard-coded. Is it really the case, or have I missed something in the documentation?

I've also attempted to modify the source to use my local server. In particular, I modified the following files:
- MTProto.php
  - Modified `RSA_KEYS` with my server's public key
  - Modified `dclist` to point to my server and port
- DataCenter.php
  - Modified the foreach at line `480` to use my server, instead of the default `X.web.telegram.web`

Unfortunately, this doesn't appear to be enough, as all requests appear to be going to Telegram servers (149.154.167.99). I've either missed something, or `composer` is doing some magic behind the scenes and caching the unmodified code somewhere.

Could someone please help me? Thanks!

title: Survive network outages: queue requests and retry reconnections
body:
Found reproducing #1921: a script whose network is cut for a minute (`docker network disconnect`) died within 30 seconds.

## Root cause

`Connection::connect()` tries each way to connect once, and throws `AssertionError: Could not connect to DC 4.0!` when all fail. It's called by whatever needs a connection: `sendMessage()` (every request) and `reconnect()` (dead connections, server errors). Called from background work, the exception escaped as an unhandled future and ended the event loop:
- `MTProtoOutgoingMessage`'s `rpc_drop_answer` for a timed-out request;
- a conference's poll;
- the reconnection of a dead connection itself.

## Fix

- `reconnect()` retries, waiting 1 s doubling to 30 s, until it connects or the connection is closed for good (a non-temporary `disconnect()`). Concurrent reconnections still each run (`ConnectRaceTest`).
- `sendMessage()` queues a message it can't send for lack of a connection, starting a reconnection if none is running: it goes out once reconnected, or times out as any request.
- `rpc_drop_answer`, best effort from the event loop, never throws.

## Verification

With #1921, five outage runs of a script with an E2E conference: it survives the minute without network every time (it died at 30 s before), and sends its queued requests once the network is back. phpunit-light passes in the trixie image (574 tests). There's no unit test of an outage: the evidence is the live runs. Bumps RELEASE to 8.13.6.

title: CLAUDE.md, skills: add the conventions only kept in memory
body:
On top of #1901: the conventions from my local memory that the PR doesn't have yet.

- **`CLAUDE.md`:**
  - **Sessions:** never SIGKILL a worker, even as a fallback in CI scripts. Workers save the session on SIGTERM, so a worker that doesn't stop is a bug to debug. Also adds valerianic's account ID.
  - **Code invariants:**
    - Warnings throw even under `@`. Any `@` in `src/` is a bug (`ErrorSuppressionTest`); use try/catch.
    - Crypto uses OpenSSL/libsodium first and phpseclib only as the fallback, with a backend comparison test. BigInteger math stays on phpseclib.
    - A response that can't be deserialized fails its request and never exits the read loop (`UndeserializableResultTest`).
  - **CI:** jobs using the CI user sessions share the `telegram-user-sessions` concurrency group.
- **Skills:**
  - **debug-ipc-hang:** the resend-forever read loop is fixed since 201ebf9ac, so a new hang of that shape is a regression. Tight loops are reproduced on a session copy instead of SIGKILLing the worker.
  - **live-ipc-tests, live-call-test:** stop workers with SIGTERM and wait. live-call-test also notes the test group ID and that the group has no invite link.
  - **release-flow:** more Telegram markdown pitfalls (the 4096 limit counts the parsed text, backticks inside a link drop it, read the entities back to check).
